version.changelog: Add UTM attribution tags (utm_source=clawhub) to ClawLink branding links so visits from this skill page are tracked as a distinct traffic source.

llm.summary: The skill has a coherent Outlook purpose, but it asks users to install and authorize a third-party ClawLink plugin with broad Microsoft account access without a pinned or verifiable plugin version.

dimensions.detail: Hosted OAuth token handling and broad mailbox/calendar/contact/task access are proportionate to an Outlook integration, but high impact and not tightly scoped in the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install instructions use a mutable package identifier, add the plugin to the allowed tools list, and restart the gateway; the artifact does not pin a reviewed version, digest, signature, or plugin source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents previews and explicit confirmation for writes, but the actual live tool catalog, OAuth scopes, and enforcement are delegated to the external ClawLink plugin/service rather than being fully specified in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup persists plugin authorization in OpenClaw configuration and relies on ClawLink retaining and injecting OAuth tokens for future Microsoft Graph requests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the capabilities: Outlook mail, calendar, contacts, tasks, attachments, rules, and sending/deleting actions through Microsoft Graph.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the ClawLink plugin and OAuth consent carefully before installing. Use a limited Microsoft account if possible, confirm every send/delete/rule/calendar write action, and know how to revoke the Microsoft connected app and remove the plugin if you no longer need it.
llm.findings:
[E4] expected: Downgraded as a false positive: the referenced 'upload session' is a Microsoft Graph large-attachment workflow, not evidence that conversation context is uploaded or exfiltrated.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a material Review concern: a third-party plugin install is expected for this integration, but the unpinned mutable package plus broad OAuth-backed Outlook authority is not sufficiently bounded or independently verifiable from the artifact.
